overview: As Assistant Secretary for Policy at the Department of Labor, Mr. And unless we bring together a whole lot of people to tell the billionaires in this country that we want an economy that works for all of us, that AI can be a good thing in healthcare and many other things. I want to share a story about AI-driven Grab-and-Go self-checkout machines at Fenway Park as an example of how technology can one lead to the loss of good middle-class jobs, two, create unintended public health and safety concerns, and three, diminished social interaction and harm cultural experience. Other things that we know are the foundations for evidence-based teaching and that through that fine tuning, through that additional training, that's how you help address some of these other challenges. And I am listening after we offered up the opportunity for the sixth time to vote in a bipartisan way to continue funding to keep our government open so that our military, federal employees all can continue to get paid and not miss a paycheck that we are coming in here to gaslight the American people and suggest that it's anything other than Democrats not voting to continue funding of our government. We see Amazon workers breaking their own backs to meet technology fuel, worksp quotas, delivery drivers whose livelihoods are determined by black box algorithms, retail workers under constant surveillance, grocery clerks replaced by machines, home health aids and housekeepers managed and fired by apps, the list goes on and on.
context: **Committee**: Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions
